recent_posts.title: Should Software Engineers Have Good Presentation Skills?
recent_posts.summary: Presentation skills matter for software engineers not as a career-climbing tactic, but as a way to share passion and inspire others. Good presentations aren't about information transfer—they're about expressing genuine enthusiasm for topics you care about, whether that's accessibility, architecture, or a technical breakthrough. Engineers already create valuable content in forums and social posts; channeling that passion into presentations or articles can have a multiplier effect. Short lightning talks of just a few minutes can spark conversations and deliver real value. The key isn't polished presentation skills—it's finding what you're passionate about and sharing it authentically.

recent_posts.title: There’s Two Sides To Every AI Tool Adoption Story
recent_posts.summary: AI coding tools like Cursor, Copilot, and CodeRabbit are transforming software development by reducing tedious work and letting engineers focus on problem-solving. While some developers resist AI due to pride or fear of appearing to cheat, those who embrace these tools demonstrably outperform those who don't. The key is identifying repetitive, time-consuming tasks in your workflow and applying AI where it makes pragmatic sense, not treating it as a universal solution. AI doesn't change the fundamentals of coding, but it dramatically reduces the effort needed to achieve results, making software engineering exciting again.

recent_posts.title: How to detect AI assistance during technical interviews
recent_posts.summary: A technical interviewer shares their experience with a candidate who appeared to be using AI assistance during the interview. The candidate gave overly detailed, buzzword-heavy answers and exhibited suspicious behaviors like reading from a screen and providing generic responses. The post includes practical tips for detecting AI usage in interviews, such as watching for consistent eye movements, overly polished language, and inability to elaborate on personal experience. It also suggests interview techniques like collaborative problem-solving and asking about confidence levels to identify authentic human responses.

recent_posts.title: How using Availability Zones can eat up your budget — our journey from Prometheus to VictoriaMetrics
recent_posts.summary: Prezi's monitoring system, originally built with Prometheus, was becoming too costly and outdated. To modernize and reduce system complexity and costs, they migrated to VictoriaMetrics. This move resulted in significant cost savings and performance improvements, with faster query times and reduced resource usage. They overcame challenges related to network traffic costs by leveraging VictoriaMetrics' efficient architecture and careful resource management, ultimately achieving a more cost-effective and scalable monitoring solution.

recent_posts.title: A Rare Insight Into The Daily Challenges Of An Experiments Team
recent_posts.summary: An experiments team, like the one at Prezi, focuses on running A/B tests to enhance product success by understanding customer behavior and improving user experience. These teams plan, implement, and evaluate tests, learning from both successful and failed experiments. Engineers in such teams need to be impact-driven, versatile, efficient, data-driven, avid learners, and comfortable with bold ideas. Effective handling of feature switches, careful planning, and thorough cleanup are crucial for maintaining code integrity and achieving meaningful results.
